prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Your Companion is Ready for Your Desktop", "Your pet is now active! Click and drag your companion anywhere on your desktop screen.", "Launch Desktop Companion"]
1: ["Name Your Desktop Pet", "Assign a custom name to seal your official adoption certificate.", "Companion Name", "Official Pet ID #4092"]
2: ["Discover Your Digital Companion", "Scroll to explore the origin story and choose your preferred adoption route.", "Select Journey"]
3: ["Sign In to Protect Your Pet", "Create or sign in to your account to securely link and save your desktop pet.", "Your pet progress is saved automatically to this account.", "Continue with Google", "Secure Cloud Sync Included"]
4: ["Signing in binds your pet identity to your account so it persists across desktop sessions."]
5: ["Choose Preset Companion or Create Custom Pet", "Select a ready-to-go companion for instant desktop setup or upload photos for a custom companion."]
6: ["Configuring desktop overlay permissions..."]
7: ["Certified Desktop Pet Owner"]
8: []
9: []
